name: Kindle-Bolt
description: The first thing every Sayer learns and the last thing most of them are good at: a spoken spark, thrown. Kindling is the loudest school because fire is the loudest thing a small voice can make.

name: Hush-Frost
description: Said under the breath, as Hush must be. The cold is not the point; the cold is what is left when the saying takes the noise out of a thing's blood and it forgets to be quick.

name: Mend
description: Mending does not close a wound. It reminds the body what shape it was in when it was last spoken of kindly, and the body, being vain, obliges.

name: Ward
description: A Binding said around yourself: a short sentence about where you end. For as long as it holds, the world argues with the sentence instead of with you.

name: Ember-Fan
description: Said outward instead of forward, so the spark does not travel but stands. Sayers teach it to anyone who has been surrounded once and did not care for it. It is not a strong saying. It is a loud one, and there are nights when loud is the whole of what you need.

name: Hearth-Brand
description: The long saying, the one the Sayers took from a Vale prayer for a fire that will not catch. Spoken at a thing instead of a hearth it does what it always did: it insists, at length, that this is the moment the burning starts.

name: Still Tongue
description: Hush does not stop a mouth. It takes the room the words would have gone into, and a saying with nowhere to land is only breath. Sayers loathe having it used on them, which is the most reliable thing anyone knows about Sayers.

name: Winter's Argument
description: A slow case, made quietly, that nothing here needs to be in such a hurry. Most things agree. The ones that do not are usually already cold.

name: Binding-Word
description: One short sentence about where a thing stops. Said at a charging boar it is the difference between a story you tell and a story told about you. It does no harm worth the name. It simply takes the next step away.

name: Keeper's Bond
description: The Wardens' own Binding, said over the one going in first. It is a promise in the grammatical sense: it holds until it is broken, and then it is only a thing somebody said.

name: Quiet the Blood
description: Not a healing. An instruction, issued firmly, to the parts of you that have become excitable. Mendings work best on things that are embarrassed to be making a fuss, which is why this one works so well on bleeding and so poorly on grief.

name: A Kind Word
description: Said over somebody else, which is harder, because you have to mean it. The Candle account says this is the whole of Mending and the rest is technique: a thing spoken of kindly holds together a little longer than it has any business doing.

name: Call the Hound
description: Every valley has a dog in it that everyone remembers and nobody owned. Calling does not make one; it asks the one already in everybody's mouth to come, and something that has been spoken of that often does not need much asking.

name: Raise the Buried
description: The Vale buries its people with the tool of their work so the ringing will know them by it. A Calling said over that ground is only a reminder of the arrangement. They come up holding the scythe. They are not pleased, and they were not pleased before, either.

name: Call a Name
description: The highest Calling and the shortest: you say a name off the Roll and wait. What comes is not the person. It is the shape a thousand evenings of being spoken of left behind, wearing the lantern and the tabard, and it will stand where you point and go out when the saying runs down. Sayers who do this often are known for being quiet afterwards.
